turns.doctor_question: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you into the clinic today?
turns.patient_response: I came in because I’ve had to be more in front of people at work, and I can’t stop focusing on this one part of my face that looks uneven in photos. Everyone tells me they barely notice it, but I see it every time.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient reports being unable to stop focusing on a perceived uneven part of their face that others barely notice.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself repeatedly checking your reflection in mirrors or other surfaces throughout the day to look at it?
turns.patient_response: Yeah. Before I send event photos or get on a vendor meeting, I keep checking my face in my phone camera. I’ll retake pictures, tilt my head different ways, or ask a coworker if I look weird. It can take up enough time that I get behind on the planning work.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient describes repeated phone-camera checking, retaking photos, altering head position, and seeking reassurance about appearance, causing interference with work planning.

turns.doctor_question: When you feel uncomfortable being in front of people at work, is that entirely because of your concern about your face, or do you also worry about other things like saying the wrong thing or embarrassing yourself?
turns.patient_response: It’s really because of my face. Since I’ve had to be more visible at work, I keep looking at that uneven part in photos, and I can’t let it go, even though other people say they barely notice it.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient attributes discomfort being visible at work to a perceived uneven facial feature that they repeatedly scrutinize in photos despite others barely noticing it.
